subject: SLO alignment & provisioning calculus for private GPU pool

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO alignment & provisioning calculus for private GPU pool

Hi team + ACME,

Following our run-through this morning, I sketched a lightweight provisioning model to map SLO targets to pool sizing (sheet attached: provisioning_calc.xlsx) and a candidate SLO matrix (slo_matrix_v1.pdf). Key asks:

- Confirm ACME's 99th-pct latency SLO target for production (are we still at 350ms for text-generation at 512 tokens?).
- Decide on buffer banding: I'm proposing a two-band model (steady + quantum burst) where the pool maintains a 20% steady headroom and a separable 50% quantum runway for short spikes (1–5 min).
- Align on networking constraints: we need explicit egress caps and minimum RTT guarantees from ACME's VPC team for queuing assumptions to hold.

Summary of the model in the spreadsheet:
- Inputs: qps profile (p50/p90/p99), mean tokens per request, target latency SLO, KV-cache hit rates.
- Output: GPU-count baseline, expected token/s throughput per GPU, warm-pool size for quantum band.

Preliminary numbers (assume text-gen model ~13B fp16):
- Baseline concurrency target: 800 concurrent requests -> ~40 token/s per request -> ~32k token/s total -> ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs baseline (quantized estimates in sheet).
- Quantum runway: additional 4 GPUs for 50% burst for up to 3 minutes without violating 99th-pct target.

Operational notes:
- If network RTT increases by >25ms we should expect a 10–15% drop in effective throughput due to queuing / head-of-line impacts.
- Cache warmup: recommend pre-warming KV caches for critical routes during business hours; warmup warm-pool in <45s target.

Next steps: can ACME confirm the latency SLO + procurement lead? Also Laura/Ben, can you review the egress assumptions in the sheet and flag anything optimistic?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO alignment & provisioning calculus for private GPU pool

Karthik — thanks for the detailed pass and the calc. A few notes after a quick read:

- Latency SLO: ACME confirmed 350ms p99 for the primary route in our call. Important: that SLO was measured with a 256-token median request; if median tokens drift to 400+ we'll need to re-run.

- Network assumptions: the egress cap in the spreadsheet is conservative (10Gb/s). For Acme's VPC we should plan for asymmetric egress throttling during peak backups and for the occasional cross-region sync. Action: Jasmine, can you validate whether the VPC peer will reserve path QoS or if we should include an additional 30% headroom?

- Queueing model: two quick points:
  * Admission control: with burst bands we need a graceful-drop policy for non-critical routes — suggest we prioritize live-chat > search > background embeddings.
  * Backpressure propagation: if the frontend starts rejecting at the edge we must have a retry/backoff shape that doesn't create synchronized retries that blow the quantum band. Consider jittered exponential backoff.

- Sizing math: your baseline of 8 GPUs looks plausible but your token/s per GPU is optimistic if we see a 15% cache miss rate. With 15% misses, baseline becomes 9–10 GPUs.

I'll add inline comments in provisioning_calc.xlsx and update the slo_matrix with two alternate scenarios (cached/uncached).

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Reliability Engineering

Quick note — I ran a micro-sim against the p99 traffic trace we collected last month. Two items:

- Reserve another 1 GPU-equivalent for safety (9–11 GPUs depending on cache behavior).
- Recommend we set the warm-pool ramp to 30s (not 45s) if we want to guarantee sub-350ms p99 under 50% burst; we can do this by keeping smaller standby VMs with preloaded weights.

Drive with sims: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-provisioning-quantum

Karthik — thanks for the clear model and the attachments. Confirming:

- ACME accepts the two-band model (20% steady + 50% quantum runway) for the initial rollout.
- p99 target: 350ms for median request sizes of up to 320 tokens. If we see sustained growth beyond that we will flag for re-sizing.
- Procurement loop: procurement@acme.example.com is now on the thread; they will start the reserved-capacity paperwork and share T&Cs.
